notes: EFFECTIVELY POSTPONED — No confirmed date. Originally targeted Aug 30, 2026. Key reasons: (1) Transitional Presidential Council (TPC) dissolved Feb 2026, leaving PM Alix Didier Fils-Aimé as sole executive authority; (2) Voter and candidate registration never began due to disputes between the Provisional Electoral Council (CEP) and PM over the electoral decree text; (3) PM designated CEP executive director as director general, concentrating control over electoral process in executive hands; (4) Electoral decree adopted June 2 but remains contentious; (5) Extreme security crisis — armed gangs control large parts of Port-au-Prince (BINUH report Jan-Mar 2026: 1,642 killed, 745 injured); (6) No candidates have formally registered. Gang Suppression Force operations ongoing but insufficient. Sources: UN Security Council Report (July 2026), BINUH, Reuters, Miami Herald.

Most closely watched German election of 2026. AfD polling near outright majority (~40-42%). CDU incumbent Schulze governs with SPD+FDP but both junior partners risk falling below 5% threshold. AfD state branch classified as confirmed right-wing extremist by domestic intelligence. AfD lead candidate Ulrich Siegmund. If firewall holds and AfD wins majority, they govern alone without needing coalition partners. Defence Minister Pistorius has discussed withholding classified info from potential AfD state ministers. Sources: Clean Energy Wire, TVP World, INSA, Politico

Riksdag election September 13, 2026. Left bloc (Social Democrats + allies) has significant lead. Andersson favored to become PM again. Immigration, defense spending, and Saab state ownership are key issues.

AfD leads as clear frontrunner (~30-35%). SPD incumbent Minister-President Manuela Schwesig personally popular but SPD weakened nationally. Same-day vote as Berlin (Sep 20). A second SPD defeat on same evening as Berlin would be devastating for Merz coalition junior partner. AfD unlikely to find coalition partners due to firewall but could complicate governance. Moscow-linked disinformation campaigns targeting eastern states reported (Euronews Jul 8). Sources: Atlantic Council, ING Think, DW

Highly fragmented five-way race. AfD topped a Berlin poll for first time (INSA Jul 23: 19%). CDU governing mayor Kai Wegner withdrew after scandal over handling of Jan 2026 power outage; replaced by Finance Senator Stefan Evers. Left Party competitive at 18%. First election with voting age 16. AfD unlikely to govern due to firewall but symbolic significance of leading in the capital. Sources: TVP World, INSA, rbb24, WSWS

Three-day voting (Sep 18-20). First Duma election since the full-scale invasion of Ukraine. Conducted under wartime conditions with significant restrictions on opposition. Sources: EPDE, RIDL, NEST Centre
